metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early January to assess progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Singapore agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 4th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is good to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have we considered January 4th for the joint meeting? It might be a good date to assess our progress. 

Also, I wonder... how do you feel about army rule? In my view, it's not as bad as some think.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
January 4th sounds like a reasonable option for the meeting. We should confirm it with everyone involved. 

As for army rule... I believe it's definitely not the way to go. In Singapore, we've seen how bad it can be. I just think it's better when people have more of a say, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I get where you're coming from, Kim. But I think, deep down, we are all the same. People are pretty much motivated by the same things, regardless of the system. It's human nature to seek stability and safety. Some values are just universal, like wanting a peaceful life. I'm sure we can find common ground on that. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I understand that perspective, but I still believe army rule limits individual freedoms and voices. It may provide stability, but at what cost? People need to be able to express themselves and participate in decision-making. That's really important for a healthy society. Common ground is good, but not at the expense of democratic values.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: It's a valid concern... but I still think that sometimes security and order come first. In many cases, people might not realize how much they need that stability until it's gone. A strong governing body can provide that. It's a different approach that can work. I guess it just depends on what you prioritize. Anyway, back to the meeting—January 4th is a solid choice, right?
